units.translation: of the evils done long ago
release the blood of deeds done long ago
this land of Apia has been called so from of old
old enemy, i.e. from long ago
for I speak of an ancient transgression
but I am a suspected enemy or one of old
τὸ παλαιόν [the olden time] in olden times
where M has παλαιάς δαίμονας [ancient divinities], the scholiast on Euripides' Alcestis 12 has παλαιάς διανομάς [ancient distributions], which I changed to παλαιάν διανομὴν [ancient distribution].
and of those advanced in age
new toils of the house mingled with old evils
the ancient ill counsel of Laius
unless some ancient deity has now changed sides with the army
the joy of the ancient vine
the ancient sins of this house
to pay for the pollution of older houses
taking the ancient image from its sanctuary
and upon me is an ancient honor
among both the younger and the older gods
with the pollutions of ancient bloodshed
and I have stepped into the ancient track
who dwell around the ancient stream of Erasinus
of these old mockeries of yours
How then can I, an old woman, learn from a younger one?
for from the gods Fate prevailed from of old
that I, old in mind, dwell beneath the earth
the great craftsman of the race, old in mind
of Orestes confessing the murder of his mother

where the scholiast says: ή μεταφορά ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῶν παλαιόντων, οἳ ἐπὶ τρισὶ πτώμασιν ὁρίζουσι τὴν ήτταν [the metaphor is from wrestlers, who determine defeat by three falls]: which Victorius explained more fully in Var. Lect. 21, 2.
this is already one of the three falls
may you have an inescapable wrestling-trick against your enemies
the metaphor is from wrestlers, who determine defeat by three falls
such a wrestler he now prepares against himself
but he was a wrestler breathing great favor toward me
a race celebrated from of old
for the heavy requitals of curses spoken of old are perfect
and among mortals an ancient saying has been established
holding the land from of old
holding the land from of old
where the scholiast says: ὁ ἐκ παλαιοῦ κληρωσάμενος τήνδε τὴν γῆν · τιμᾶται γὰρ παρὰ Θηβαίοις ὁ ῎Αρης [the one who from of old obtained this land by lot; for Ares is honored among the Thebans].
Ares who holds the land from of old
the one who from of old obtained this land by lot; for Ares is honored among the Thebans
for I am the son of earth-born Palaechthon, Pelasgus
